name: php-db
description: A PHP application or packaged product with its own relational database (for example MariaDB or MySQL), served through a web server's PHP handler.

runtimes.provision: <installed on dev and prod hosts; never committed to the repo>
<installed separately; its data directory is state, restored from backup, never committed>

build.command: composer install --no-dev  (only if the app uses composer)
<copy the app's own extensions or config templates into place>

services.port: <the database's port; keep it out of the web app's own port range>
services.start: <the database server as a managed service, with its data directory outside the repo>
services.bind: <loopback-only, unless the app tier runs on a different host>

services.start: <PHP under the web server's own PHP handler, or a PHP-served web process under a service manager>
services.manager: <a service manager or the web server itself>
services.bind: <loopback-only, unless a trusted edge forwards identity>
services.health: <a page that exercises PHP and the database together>

routing.note: decide the login design before anything else: an in-app login sitting behind a shared authenticating edge can loop unless the app has its own routing prefix that bypasses that edge

files: <the product's config file, e.g. a config-*.php or .env>
config.rule: holds database credentials: template it with placeholders, never commit the real one

data.migrations: <the product's own upgrade path, or hand-written SQL migrations>
data.state: the database itself: a backup and restore plan is required before go-live

ci.workflow: <CI workflow file: PHP lint, the app's own tests, package the customisation>
requiredJobs: <to decide, based on what the app already tests>

verify: a page that exercises PHP and the database returns real content, not a generic error page
the login flow reaches the app
